vicious: The vicious wind blew my hat right across the beach.
What a vicious gust that was, flipping our picnic blanket over!
The sea looked vicious that day, with huge waves crashing on the rocks.
precious: Water is precious in the desert, so we must not waste a drop.
She wrapped the precious photograph of her gran in soft paper.
Every minute of our holiday felt precious, so we played until dark.
gracious: Even though she lost the game, she stayed gracious and clapped for the winner.
A gracious host welcomes every guest and offers them a drink.
How gracious she was, thanking each person who helped at the fair!
spacious: Our new classroom is spacious, so everyone has room to spread out.
The spacious boot of the car held all our bags and a tent.
Is your bedroom spacious enough for a bunk bed and a desk?
cautious: She was cautious on the icy path and took small, slow steps.
Dad is cautious when he tries a new recipe, so he reads it twice.
Be cautious on the wet steps and hold the rail.
delicious: These biscuits taste so delicious that I want another one!
The delicious smell of toast drifted up the stairs to my bed.
Is the chocolate cake as delicious as it looks?
ambitious: She is ambitious and practises piano every morning to win first prize.
Are you ambitious enough to try for the top spot in the school quiz?
It was an ambitious plan to build a huge tree house in one day.
nutritious: Milk and cheese are nutritious foods that help your bones grow strong.
Our nutritious soup was packed with vegetables to help us stay strong and healthy.
Is a school lunch with salad and fish nutritious enough to keep you healthy?
suspicious: I felt suspicious when my brother smiled and hid something behind his back.
Mum felt suspicious when she saw crumbs and the empty biscuit tin.
A suspicious rustle came from the cupboard, so I peeked inside.
infectious: The giggles were infectious, and soon the whole class was laughing.
Yawning is infectious, so when one person yawns, we all do.
His happy singing was infectious, and everyone clapped along.

rejected.s: In the pantomime, the villain had a vicious laugh and a cruel plan.
rejected.reason: checker: Infectious laugh is a common phrase, and suspicious laugh also works, so the gap is unclear. (also fits: infectious, suspicious)

rejected.s: Why was the storm so vicious that it snapped the garden fence?
rejected.reason: checker: The 'Why was it so... that' wording is awkward and unnatural for a child.

rejected.s: My grandad's old watch is precious to him, so he keeps it safe.
rejected.reason: machine rule 4: not on the word lists: grandad's

rejected.s: It was gracious of Dad to thank everyone politely after the party.
rejected.reason: machine rule 4: capital word not allowed: Dad

rejected.s: Why are you so cautious about standing on that wobbly stool?
rejected.reason: checker: It treats being careful as odd and suggests standing on a wobbly stool, which is unsafe.

rejected.s: The cautious rabbit sniffed the air before hopping out of its hutch.
rejected.reason: checker: A suspicious rabbit sniffing the air also makes sense. (also fits: suspicious)

rejected.s: Mum baked a delicious apple pie, and the whole kitchen smelled sweet.
rejected.reason: checker: Having Mum do the baking repeats a stereotype about who cooks.

rejected.s: We ate delicious fish and chips on the seafront.
rejected.reason: checker: There is no taste clue, so nutritious could also fill the gap. (also fits: nutritious)

rejected.s: A bowl of porridge with fruit is a nutritious start to the day.
rejected.reason: checker: A delicious start to the day also fits well. (also fits: delicious)

rejected.s: Choose a nutritious snack, such as an apple, to give you energy.
rejected.reason: checker: A delicious snack such as an apple also makes sense. (also fits: delicious)

rejected.s: Her excitement about the trip was so infectious that we all cheered.
rejected.reason: machine rule 5: shares a run of 4 words with the example

rejected.s: What an infectious tune, because now we are all humming it!
